root_cause.text: `ksmbd`’s `smb_check_perm_dacl()` validated only that enough bytes remained for an ACE header, but failed to enforce the minimum on-wire ACE size before reading `access_req` and `sid`, allowing crafted ACL entries with undersized `ace->size` to trigger out-of-bounds reads in the DACL-walking loops.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces the weak check `offsetof(struct smb_ace, access_req) > aces_size` / `ace_size > aces_size` with a minimum-size requirement `ace_size < offsetof(struct smb_ace, sid) + CIFS_SID_BASE_SIZE`, and also adds `if (ace->sid.num_subauth > SID_MAX_SUB_AUTHORITIES) break;` before `compare_sids()`, matching the CVE description that `access_req` and `ace->sid` were read OOB when `ace->size == 4`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Harden DACL ACE parsing by rejecting malformed or truncated ACE records before permission evaluation.
intent_record.what: In smb_check_perm_dacl(), the ACE parsing loop changed its bounds checks: the pre-read check now tests whether the remaining ACL data is large enough to contain at least a SID by comparing `offsetof(struct smb_ace, sid) + aces_size` against `CIFS_SID_BASE_SIZE`, and the per-ACE size validation now rejects ACEs not only when `ace_size > aces_size` but also when `ace_size` is smaller than `offsetof(struct smb_ace, sid) + CIFS_SID_BASE_SIZE`.
intent_record.how: This tightens validation of ACL entries before they are parsed and used. At runtime, malformed or truncated ACEs that do not contain a full SID, or that claim an invalidly small size, will now cause the loop to stop instead of being processed, reducing the risk of out-of-bounds reads or incorrect permission evaluation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Tighten ACE parsing in SMB DACL permission checks with additional size and SID-structure validation to safely reject malformed ACL entries.
intent_record.what: The DACL permission-check loop adds stricter bounds validation for each ACE: it replaces the old `access_req` size check with a check that the ACE still contains at least a base SID (`sid` plus `CIFS_SID_BASE_SIZE`), rejects ACEs whose declared `ace_size` is either larger than the remaining ACL bytes or smaller than the minimum SID-containing size, and adds a new check that `ace->sid.num_subauth` does not exceed `SID_MAX_SUB_AUTHORITIES`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, malformed or truncated ACE entries in the ACL will now cause the loop to stop before the code attempts to compare SIDs from invalid memory or process structurally corrupt ACEs. This reduces the risk of out-of-bounds reads and prevents invalid ACL data from being treated as a valid permission entry.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is an undersized ACE being accepted after checking only that enough bytes remain for an ACE header, leading to out-of-bounds reads of `access_req` and `sid`. In this function, the DACL-walking loops explicitly validate the ACE size before dereferencing fields: `if (offsetof(struct smb_ace, access_req) > aces_size) break;` followed by `ace_size = le16_to_cpu(ace->size); if (ace_size > aces_size) break;` and then only after that do they read `ace->access_req` / `ace->sid`. This means the minimum on-wire size is enforced here, so the vulnerable construct is not present in this commit version. Because the fix is already present in the shown code, `is_fixed` is YES.
